claims.text: Add DumpAnchors() when deactivating network to persist anchors immediately rather than waiting for shutdown.
claims.quote: Have you considered also adding a DumpAnchors() if anchors_to_dump.size() > 1 when setting network active from true to false?
claims.status_note: author deferred dumping anchors on network deactivation to a follow-up PR
claims.status_by_quote: Yes, but would leave it for a follow-up, it will require more changes than the simple ones to cover the `-networkactive` behavior.

claims.text: Document in the setnetworkactive RPC that setting fNetworkActive to false can prevent anchors from being preserved.
claims.quote: it may be better to document that setting `fNetworkActive` to false via the `setnetworkactive` RPC can prevent anchors from being preserved.
claims.status_note: author added documentation to the setnetworkactive RPC

claims.text: Harden anchor logic to avoid deleting anchors when disconnected from the internet even if networkactive is not set to 0.
claims.quote: I wonder if we should harden it a bit to make sure that we don’t delete anchors if `networkactive` is not set, but the user is not connected to the internet.
claims.status_note: author clarified the scope is user-disabled networking rather than detecting network loss
claims.status_by_quote: To clarify, I don't think this is exploitable, it is mostly about the own user restarting the node

claims.text: Load anchors at startup even when network activity is disabled, avoid popping them while inactive, and save them on exit.
claims.quote: shouldn't anchors be loaded at startup even if networkactive is false and maybe just skip saving them if network is inactive?
claims.status_note: author overhauled the PR approach to preserve anchors when starting with network disabled or disabling via RPC
claims.status_by_quote: I just changed the approach of this PR and changed PR title and description. It addresses concerns like https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34213#discussion_r2718514479. Now this PR addresses cases involving disabling network via RPC and starting the node with the network disabled via flag.

claims.text: Disabling network activity drops existing anchors on a subsequent clean shutdown if no new connections were made.
claims.quote: This seems like a bug... Maybe we should re-save the original anchors if there's no new ones at a clean shutdown?
claims.status_note: author overhauled PR approach to preserve anchors across network deactivation and clean shutdown
claims.status_by_quote: I just changed the approach of this PR and changed PR title and description. It addresses concerns like https://github.c

claims.text: Whether anchors should be restored if the user subsequently uses setnetworkactive to enable network.
claims.quote: If the user subsequently uses `setnetworkactive` to enable network, should we restore the anchors then?
claims.status_note: author agreed and deferred restoring anchors on network enable to a follow-up PR
claims.status_by_quote: Yes, I think so. I will implement it in a follow-up.

claims.text: Maintain m_anchors by swapping in current working block-only connections while retaining old addresses if insufficient connections exist.
claims.quote: I think maintaining `m_anchors` as something like: ... could work? ie update it with the address of current blocks-only connections that have been working, but if there aren't any (or enough) such connections, keep the old addresses.
claims.status_note: author proposed instead saving active anchors to m_anchors on network deactivation
claims.status_by_quote: Perhaps when disabling the network, we could save the anchors (we're connected to) to `m_anchors` and use it in `StopNodes`

claims.text: Update documentation of m_anchors to reflect new usage and append rather than replace anchors when disabling network.
claims.quote: The docs of m_anchors should be updated to reflect this. Also, it would make sense here to append to m_anchors, instead of substituting
claims.status_note: author updated m_anchors documentation but declined appending anchors for now
claims.status_by_quote: I've changed the documentation of `m_anchors` according to the new behavior ... Left this as is for now

claims.text: A race condition between setting fNetworkActive to false and socket disconnection allows ThreadSocketHandler to clear connections before block-relay peers are captured into m_anchors.
claims.quote: currently there is a data race, you should first save the anchors, and only then set `fNetworkActive = active`
claims.status_note: author reordered operations to capture anchors before setting fNetworkActive to false
claims.status_by_quote: Fixed data race when disabling the network and saving the anchors.

claims.text: Add AssertLockNotHeld assertions for m_anchors at the start of relevant functions.
claims.quote: You should add a `AssertLockNotHeld` at the start of the function, similarly to `AssertLockNotHeld(m_reconnections_mutex);`
claims.status_note: author added AssertLockNotHeld assertions for m_anchors

claims.text: ThreadOpenConnections continues popping and discarding anchors while network activity is disabled, leading to empty anchors upon shutdown.
claims.quote: ThreadOpenConnections() still consumes m_anchors while networking is disabled. It pops an address before calling OpenNetworkConnection(), which then returns because fNetworkActive is false.
claims.status_note: author pushed fix skipping anchor logic when network is inactive
claims.status_by_quote: Looks pretty nice to me now, thanks for addressing my comments.

claims.text: Anchors saved on network deactivation were not capped to the oldest peers, allowing a newly added block-relay peer to displace older anchors.
claims.quote: GetCurrentBlockRelayOnlyConns() returns peers in connection order, while ThreadOpenConnections() consumes anchors from the back... Including a temporary third peer therefore lets it take the oldest anchor’s place after a network toggle.
claims.status_note: author capped anchors saved on network deactivation to MAX_BLOCK_RELAY_ONLY_ANCHORS

claims.text: Skip the ThreadOpenConnections loop body entirely while the network is inactive to avoid redundant addrman Select() calls.
claims.quote: Maybe ThreadOpenConnections should skip its loop body entirely while the network is inactive.

support.reason: I think this is a good improvement, makes sense to have, and I can’t find any additional surface of attack introduced here... low risk, and would avoid unnecessarily losing anchors.

Disabling networking should not cause the node to lose its anchors. Preserving them across a clean shutdown lets the node reconnect when networking resumes, increasing eclipse attack resilience on restarts.
Tested changes with 3 scenarios before and after changes.
